confirmed: Owned, bounded native wake reservations expose earliest deadline, revision and unread wake events
Native management syscall and userspace wrapper query the wake registry under resource-management authority
Dropping the last timer handle releases its reservation; unread expirations keep a wake event pending
Native wall-clock observers rebase absolute timers or deliver a cancellation; stale callbacks are rejected
Linux CAP_WAKE_ALARM translates into Shield RESERVE_WAKE; create and rearm require it
Stock Bionic creates REALTIME_ALARM and BOOTTIME_ALARM timerfds, receives epoll events, reads expirations and creates a disarmed CANCEL_ON_SET monitor
A forked process after setuid cannot create or rearm wake timers
Timerfd records safely cross user page boundaries and reject unmapped tails
Stock SystemServer completes AlarmManagerService and reaches InputManagerService
ProcessScope teardown leaves no live members

current_stop.message: Input must be able to block suspend to properly process events
current_stop.cause: CAP_BLOCK_SUSPEND is not advertised because native suspend-inhibition and EPOLLWAKEUP enforcement are not implemented
current_stop.approved_next: Lifetime-owned native suspend-inhibition tokens coordinated with outer power management, including conservative inhibition throughout EPOLLWAKEUP registration until input wake sources are supported.

limits: The registry reports software-only scheduling. No hardware wake source or physical suspend/resume support is claimed
Wall-clock discontinuity handling is covered by native unit tests; physical RTC stepping during suspend is not tested
No Android application frame or home screen is confirmed
